clue.text: Carl's acted in play "The tangled string"

indicators.note: words put in play are moved about freely, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: the possessive's S counts here as a letter of the fodder

explanation.surface: A man called Carl took a part in a stage show called The Tangled String.
explanation.walkthrough: The quotation marks make it look like a play's title, but the title itself is the definition. 'in play' tells you to rearrange the letters of CARL'S ACTED.
explanation.definitionFit: This children's game is played by looping a length of yarn between the fingers and passing the knotted figures from hand to hand.

clue.text: Fellow has to stand up

explanation.surface: A man has to get to his feet.
explanation.definitionFit: Old cock is a familiar British term for a chap; to tilt something upright, as a dog does its ears, is the verb sense.

clue.text: Heard 22 drop

indicators.note: heard means the word is said aloud and the letters entered are those of a word sounding the same

parts.note: the answer to 22 down is TIER, a row

explanation.surface: Listen to number 22 fall.
explanation.walkthrough: 22 down gives TIER, which sounds like a word for a drop of liquid from the eye.
explanation.definitionFit: A single bead of salty fluid shed when crying is a teardrop.

clue.text: Quarrelsome one quits espionage agency over intelligence about ship

indicators.note: over in a down clue means this piece sits above the rest
one quits says the letter for one leaves the word

parts.note: the CIA is the American spy agency
the Roman numeral for one is I

indicators.note: about says one piece goes around the other

parts.note: nous is common sense or intelligence
a tanker is a ship carrying oil

explanation.surface: A bad-tempered officer leaves the spy service over news of a vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'quits' removes I from CIA to leave CA, placed 'over' NOUS wrapped 'about' TANKER.
explanation.definitionFit: A cantankerous person is irritable and argumentative, always ready for a row.

clue.text: Bill, a rising player

parts.note: a bill is an account, abbreviated AC from a/c
a tor is a rocky hill, a rising of ground

explanation.surface: A man called Bill is a promising performer on the way up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rising' looks like a reversal signal in a down clue, but 'a rising' is a noun for a hill or tor. Bill is not a name but an account.
explanation.definitionFit: A performer on stage is someone who plays a part.

clue.text: Poet's expression of surprise about black boy

definitions.note: the 's stands for is, joining the definition to the wordplay

indicators.note: about says one piece goes around the other

parts.note: Lordy is an exclamation of astonishment
B is an abbreviation for black, as on pencils
Ron is a boy's name

explanation.surface: A writer of verse gasps at a dark-haired lad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poet's' is the definition, with 's meaning is; 'about' sets the black letter inside the exclamation.
explanation.definitionFit: This Romantic writer of Don Juan was one of the best-known English poets.

clue.text: Diplomacy changed direction, we hear

indicators.note: we hear says the letters come from a word said out loud, not as written

parts.note: a sailing boat that changes direction against the wind has tacked

explanation.surface: A negotiator's tactful approach shifted course, so the rumour goes.
explanation.walkthrough: TACKED, a sailing term for turning into the wind, is said aloud and sounds the same as the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words mean skill in handling people without causing offence.

clue.text: Non-essential note accompanying volume I on teeth

parts.note: A is a musical note
cc, cubic centimetres, is a measure of volume
dental means concerning the teeth

explanation.surface: A musical extra sounds as tooth-related work goes on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'note' tempts as part of the definition, a musical accidental, but it gives A. 'accompanying' just joins the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Something incidental, arising by chance, is not a necessary part of the whole.

clue.text: Cleaner used excessively in the past

parts.note: too means excessively, as in too much

indicators.note: in says one piece goes inside the other

explanation.surface: Something for cleaning was used too much in earlier times.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' sets the synonym for past inside the word the, between its second and third letters. 'used' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: The paste squeezed onto a brush is a cleanser for teeth.

clue.text: Restrictions damaged part of commercial empire

parts.note: chains are restraints that limit movement
tore is the past tense of tear, to damage by ripping

explanation.surface: Regulations hurt one branch of a large business.
explanation.walkthrough: 'damaged' looks like an anagram signal working on 'Restrictions', but it is a plain synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: A retail group runs many identical shops, each a branch of the larger business.

clue.text: A nymph to follow slavishly

explanation.surface: A mythical spirit is told to trail after someone like a servant.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth a mountain spirit pined for Narcissus until only her voice remained; the verb means to repeat or copy someone else exactly.

clue.text: Park edict -it's broken in a National Park

indicators.note: broken means the letters are smashed up and rearranged

parts.note: the S of it's counts as a letter of the fodder

explanation.surface: A park order is breached inside one of Britain's protected areas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broken' tells you to rearrange PARK EDICT IT'S. The answer is the English national park in Derbyshire.
explanation.definitionFit: This upland region in Derbyshire, England was the first area to be made a protected national reserve, in 1951.

clue.text: Harsh beard-it is reduced to a whisker

indicators.note: a thing reduced to pieces is broken up, so these letters are rearranged into new order

explanation.surface: A rough growth of beard is trimmed down to stubble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reduced to' looks like shaving advice; it tells you to rearrange HARSH BEARD IT. 'is' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Both phrases mean the smallest possible margin, as in winning by a tiny distance.

clue.text: Opossum may be in difficulties

explanation.surface: A marsupial may be in trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: A marsupial up a eucalyptus is literal; the idiom means stuck in an awkward predicament.

clue.text: Disputing a proverb that supports profit

indicators.note: that supports in a down clue means this piece sits under the other

parts.note: gain means profit
a saying is a proverb

explanation.surface: Arguing that an adage backs up making money.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry, a piece that supports another comes beneath it.
explanation.definitionFit: To contradict or deny a statement is to argue against it.

clue.text: Playing partners holding king and joker

indicators.note: holding says one piece is placed inside the other
letters playing about are moved around, so the word partners is rearranged

parts.note: K is the standard abbreviation for king, as in chess notation

explanation.surface: Two people at a card table keep hold of the king and the joker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'holding' puts K inside PRANSTER, a rearrangement of PARTNERS signalled by 'Playing'.
explanation.definitionFit: A practical jester who plays tricks on others is a joker.

clue.text: Somewhat superior to a bird, an amphibian, say

indicators.note: superior to in a down clue means the earlier pieces sit above this one

parts.note: a toad is an amphibian
say means for example, abbreviated EG
a ree is a female ruff, a wading bird

explanation.surface: A frog or similar creature rates a little higher than a bird.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry 'superior to' puts TOAD and EG above REE, an old name for the female ruff, a wading bird. 'say' gives EG, not a sound signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Both mean to some extent, partially rather than completely.

clue.text: Country's name included in important article

definitions.note: the 's stands for is, joining the definition to the wordplay

indicators.note: included in says one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: key means important, as in a key witness
a is the indefinite article in grammar

explanation.surface: A nation's title appears in a significant newspaper piece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'included in' puts N inside KEY to make KENY, then A follows.
explanation.definitionFit: This East African nation, with Nairobi as its capital, is a country.

clue.text: Not the Italian king's daughter -she's beyond help

indicators.note: not with a piece means that piece is taken away

parts.note: in Shakespeare's King Lear the king's eldest daughter is Goneril
il is the Italian word for the

explanation.surface: Someone who is not a princess from Italy is a lost cause.
explanation.walkthrough: The king is Lear: remove IL from his daughter GONERIL. The surface suggests an Italian royal, but 'the Italian' just gives IL.
explanation.definitionFit: A person or thing past saving or doomed is said to be done for.

clue.text: I get regular payments — an exotic night with a good book

parts.note: nuit is French for night, a foreign word for it
NT is the New Testament, part of the Good Book, the Bible

explanation.surface: A pensioner with a steady income spends a romantic foreign evening with a fine read.
explanation.walkthrough: 'exotic' signals a foreign word rather than an anagram: French NUIT. The definition speaks in the first person as the answer itself.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who receives a yearly sum under an insurance contract or pension is paid at regular intervals.

clue.text: Dimensions of certain people overwhelmed by things to eat

indicators.note: overwhelmed by says one piece is engulfed by the other, so it sits inside

parts.note: meats are foods, things to eat
sure means certain
men means people, as in men and women of a crew

explanation.surface: Some people's sizes increase because of all the food they consume.
explanation.walkthrough: 'overwhelmed by' means the certain people end up surrounded by the food, which splits after its third letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Sizes taken with a tape, such as chest and waist, are a person's figures.

clue.text: Come in with chips but no fish

indicators.note: but no says the fish is removed from the word

parts.note: Chips is the traditional nickname for a ship's carpenter
a carp is a freshwater fish

explanation.surface: Arrive with fries, but no fish to go with them.
explanation.walkthrough: The fish and chips picture misleads; Chips is a carpenter's nickname. Remove CARP from CARPENTER.
explanation.definitionFit: To go into a room or building is to step inside.

clue.text: Row about it escalates

indicators.note: escalates means climbs, so in a down clue the pieces are read upwards

parts.note: re means about, concerning

explanation.surface: An argument about something intensifies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'escalates' turns RE and IT upwards together in this down entry. 'Row' tempts as a quarrel, but it means a line of seats.
explanation.definitionFit: One level in a stack or a line of seats rising above another is a row.

clue.text: Basil, for instance — a bachelor after a girl

indicators.note: after says the bachelor's letter comes behind the girl

parts.note: her refers to a girl

explanation.surface: A man named Basil, a single fellow, pursues a young woman.
explanation.walkthrough: Basil looks like a man's name, but here it is the kitchen plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Basil is an aromatic leaf used in cooking, one example of this plant group.

clue.text: Not entirely regretting downfall

indicators.note: not entirely means the word is cut short by its last letter

parts.note: to rue is to regret, so regretting is ruing

explanation.surface: Someone half-sorry about their collapse.
explanation.walkthrough: RUING (regretting) loses its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Both mean a collapse or destruction, as in a business brought to its knees.

clue.text: Drifter involved with CIA related killing

indicators.note: involved means mixed up together, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A vagrant mixed up with American spies commits a murder within the family.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involved' asks you to rearrange DRIFTER and CIA together; 'with' just joins them.
explanation.definitionFit: Killing one's own brother is a murder of a blood relative.

clue.text: To some extent seed gets an advantage

indicators.note: To some extent says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A tournament seeding gives a player something of a head start.
explanation.definitionFit: Having the upper hand over a rival means holding a lead or benefit.

clue.text: Thief primarily breaks into home to steal the object of one's love

indicators.note: breaks into says one piece goes inside the other, as a burglar enters a house

parts.note: the hearth stands for the home, as in hearth and home

indicators.note: primarily means the first letter of the word Thief is used

parts.note: to rob is to steal

explanation.surface: A burglar enters a house to take away a beloved possession.
explanation.walkthrough: 'primarily' takes the first letter of Thief, which 'breaks into' the home as a burglar would; the word for steal follows.
explanation.definitionFit: A dreamy idol adored by fans is someone others are infatuated with.
